channel.title: Cadence Evidence — PT Research Signal
channel.description: Daily curated physical therapy & rehab research for clinicians. AI-scored signal from 56 sources.

item.title: Rehabilitation of Athletes With Hamstring Strain Injury: SONAFE-Brazil Clinical Practice Guideline.
item.description: The National Society of Sports Physical Therapy (SONAFE-Brazil) released a clinical practice guideline using the GRADE approach to address rehabilitation interventions for hamstring strain injury in athletes, synthesizing evidence from randomized clinical trials.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Effects of treadmill exercise with and without vertical traction on gait, pain, disability, trunk proprioception, and depression in patients with chronic mechanical low back pain: A randomized controlled trial.
item.description: A randomized controlled trial (n=45) found that adding vertical traction and partial body weight support to treadmill exercise (VT+TE) significantly improved TUG performance, self-selected gait speed, disability, and flexion/extension repositioning errors more than treadmill exercise alone (TE) or core stabilization in patients with chronic mechanical low back pain. Both VT+TE and TE improved pain and depressive symptoms.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Long-Term Clinical Outcomes and Factors Associated With Response in Older Adults With Massive Irreparable Rotator Cuff Tears: A Four-Year Prospective Cohort Study.
item.description: A 4-year prospective cohort study of 92 older adults with atraumatic massive irreparable rotator cuff tears found that 76 patients showed clinically important improvements with nonoperative treatment (physical therapy, home exercises, NSAIDs, and corticosteroid injection) that persisted for 4 years. Smoking and longer symptom duration were associated with worse shoulder function.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Efficacy of Sensory Electrical Stimulation Versus Alternating Electromyography-Guided Electrical Stimulation on Functional Recovery of the Hand in Chronic Stroke: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
item.description: A three-arm randomized controlled trial (n=60) in chronic stroke patients found that both sensory electrical stimulation (SES) and alternating electromyography-guided electrical stimulation (Alt-EMG), combined with conventional physical therapy, significantly improved upper-limb motor function (adjusted mean gains of 12.05 and 12.44 points on ARAT, respectively, versus control, both P < .001) over 12 weeks, with no significant difference between SES and Alt-EMG.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Photobiomodulation therapy has a negligible effect as an adjunct to motor control exercise in people with chronic non-specific low back pain: a randomised trial.
item.description: A randomized controlled trial of 148 participants found that adding photobiomodulation therapy (PBMT) to motor control exercise (MCE) provided negligible additional improvements in pain intensity (MD -0.4 points, 95% CI -1.2 to 0.4) and disability (MD -0.7 points, 95% CI -2.4 to 0.9) compared to sham PBMT plus MCE for chronic non-specific low back pain over 12 months.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Association Between Early Postoperative Limb Symmetry Index Scores and 2-Year Patient-Reported Outcomes After Quadriceps Tendon Autograft ACL Reconstruction.
item.description: In 100 patients after QT-ACLR, 3-month isometric quadriceps LSI scores significantly predicted 2-year IKDC scores (β = 3.9; Adj R2 = 0.36; P < .03), with patients achieving PASS having higher LSI scores.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Post burn Cubital Tunnel Syndrome Electrophysiological and Functional Responses to High intensity Laser Therapy versus Extracorporeal Shock Wave Therapy: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
item.description: A randomized controlled trial (n=75) found high-intensity laser therapy (HILT) combined with ulnar nerve gliding exercises (UNGE) significantly improved ulnar motor nerve conduction velocity, CMAP amplitudes, and DASH scores compared to ESWT+UNGE or UNGE alone, with benefits maintained at 12-week follow-up.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Reframing hands-on musculoskeletal assessment as a measurement instrument rather than a technique debate: a theoretical framework applying COSMIN to HODA-A.
item.description: This theoretical paper proposes the Hands-On Data Acquisition and Analysis (HODA-A) framework for conceptualizing hands-on musculoskeletal examination as a clinician-reported outcome measurement process, applying COSMIN principles to establish a foundation for validation research.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Effects of thoracic kinesiological taping on pulmonary functions, respiratory muscle strength, and functional independence in patients with hemiplegia: a randomized controlled clinical trial.
item.description: A randomized controlled trial of 30 chronic stroke hemiplegia patients found that thoracic kinesiology taping (KT) combined with conventional rehabilitation significantly improved pulmonary function (FVC, FEV1, PEF all p < 0.001), inspiratory muscle strength (MIP p < 0.001), and functional independence (FIM p = 0.029) compared to sham taping.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Comparison of kinesio taping and myofascial release therapy in cervicogenic headache: a randomized controlled trial.
item.description: A randomized controlled trial of 81 cervicogenic headache patients found that both kinesio taping (KT) and myofascial release (MFR) combined with home exercise significantly improved pain, disability, quality of life, and headache frequency compared to home exercise alone. MFR showed more sustained improvements in disability and physical quality of life.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Client Challenge
item.description: An umbrella review of 28 meta-analyses found that exercise-containing interventions consistently supported improvements in muscle function and physical performance in older adults, particularly for fall-related outcomes. Nutrition-only interventions showed modest benefits for muscle mass in selected vulnerable populations, while combined interventions improved some strength and functional outcomes.
item.author: BMC Geriatrics

item.title: Effectiveness of conservative interventions on pain and disability in degenerative cervical spine disease: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 18 RCTs (2,378 participants) on degenerative cervical spine disease found that conservative interventions significantly reduced pain (SMD = −0.67, 95% CI: −0.97 to −0.37) and disability (SMD = −0.60, 95% CI: −0.97 to −0.24). Acupuncture and exercise-based interventions showed significant benefits, while manual therapy did not demonstrate a significant pooled benefit. The certainty of evidence was low.
item.author: BMC Musculoskelet Disord

item.title: Effects of Exercise Training on the Metabolic Cost of Walking in Health and Disease: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 27 studies (1,177 participants) found that chronic physical exercise training improved the metabolic cost of walking (Cw) (g = 0.40, p = 0.001) across healthy adults and individuals with neurological conditions. Improvements were significant in healthy individuals (g = 0.49, p = 0.001) but smaller in stroke patients (g = 0.24, p = 0.065). Population moderated the effects of training on Cw (p = 0.043), with higher BMI associated with smaller effects.
item.author: Sports Medicine

item.title: Modality-specific, deficit-targeted exercise prescriptions for physical function in sarcopenia and frailty: a network meta-analysis
item.description: A network meta-analysis of 61 RCTs (3,706 participants) on sarcopenia and frailty found that multicomponent training with resistance training offered the most comprehensive benefits for functional mobility (low certainty). Elastic band resistance training was most effective for handgrip strength (MD 1.95 kg; 95% CI, 1.13 to 2.76; moderate certainty), and machine-based resistance training showed intermediate effectiveness for knee extension strength (MD 2.96 kg; 95% CI, 1.59 to 4.34; low certainty).
item.author: BMC Geriatrics

item.title: Efficacy of physiotherapy in reducing pain in subjects with temporomandibular disorders: a systematic review with network meta-analysis
item.description: A systematic review and network meta-analysis of 25 RCTs (1,540 participants) found that manual therapy and therapeutic exercise are effective in reducing pain in temporomandibular disorders. Multimodal treatments, particularly combining dry needling and manual therapy, appeared to be the most effective approach.
item.author: medRxiv

item.title: Can Psychological Readiness Predict Successful Return to Sports After Patellar Stabilization Surgery in Adolescent Patients? A Retrospective Cohort Study.
item.description: In adolescent patients (n=97) after patellar stabilization surgery, an ACL-RSI score ≥59.2 was found to be an independent predictor (odds ratio, 3.56; 95% CI, 1.10-11.51; P = .033) for successful return to sport (78.3% achieved RTS).
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Digital therapeutic combining exercise and cognitive-behavioural therapy reduces pain in patients with chronic patellofemoral pain: a multicentre randomised controlled trial
item.description: A multicentre randomized controlled trial showed that a smartphone-based multidisciplinary intervention combining personalized exercise and cognitive-behavioral therapy significantly improved pain, function, quality of life, and psychological well-being in patients with chronic patellofemoral pain.
item.author: BJSM

item.title: Six-month supervised telerehabilitation combining pilates-based therapeutic exercise and self-myofascial release in adults with fibromyalgia: a randomized controlled trial | Journal of Rehabilitation Medicine
item.description: A 6-month randomized controlled trial (N=68) found that supervised multicomponent telerehabilitation combining Pilates-based therapeutic exercise and self-myofascial release significantly improved fibromyalgia impact, sleep quality, depressive symptoms, and perceived stress (p < 0.001 to 0.028) compared to usual care, with 87.5% adherence and no adverse events.
item.author: J Rehabil Med

item.title: Do treatment parameters of dry needling influence its effect on pain? A systematic review and meta-analysis.
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 71 comparisons (23 for quantitative synthesis) on dry needling for neck pain found no significant influence of treatment parameters (number of sessions, muscles treated, or local twitch responses) on pain outcomes (QM = 0.26, p = 0.968 to QM = 3.17, p = 0.205). The evidence does not support a reliable dose-response relationship.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: From information to action; co-designing pain neuroscience education for adolescents with low back pain: Focus group insights.
item.description: A co-design study with 15 adolescents (15-19 years old) with low back pain found that effective pain neuroscience education (PNE) material should be back-specific, practical, trustworthy, and presented in an engaging format adapted to young people's preferences. These insights guided the development of the "Back To Move" prototype.
item.author: PubMed
